```{r}
library(circular)
library(tidyverse)
```

Correct model (from Friday 10/30):
```{r}
set.seed(1)

# predictors
n <- 5000
x <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n), x3 = rnorm(n))

# parameters
k <- 5 
beta <- c(0,0.5, 0.5) #starting simple
beta0 <- 2

# calculating linear predictors and conditional mean directions
xb <- as.vector(as.matrix(x) %*% beta)

# link function -> mu = 2arctan(xbeta), when we run it through this, we are getting back to the angles
mu <- beta0 + 2 * atan(xb) 

# generate circular responses from VM dist
y <- sapply(mu, function(m) {
  as.numeric(rvonmises(1, mu = circular(m), kappa = k))
})

# visualizing simulated responses using rose diagram
rose.diag(circular(y), bins = 24, col = "mediumvioletred")

# creating simulated dataset
sim_data <- data.frame(x, y)
#head(sim_data)

# linear regression
mod1 <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = sim_data)
summary(mod1)

# circular regression
mod2 <- lm.circular(y = circular(y), x = as.matrix(x), type = "c-l", init = c(0, 0, 0))

```

Testing diff vals of kappa for lin vs cir reg
want to answer the question: as kappa changes, how does the circular estimate change from the linear estimate?

using one predictor, n = 500, true beta = 0.1, intercept = 2, different values of kappa, estimate slope for linear kappa and circular kappa
```{r}
set.seed(1)
# parameters
n <- 500
beta0 <- 2
beta <- 2

# (methods research) different values of kappa based on:
# 0 - uniform dist around circle
# 0.5 - very low concentration
# 1 - low concentration
# 5 - moderate concentration
# 10 - high concentration
# 20 - very high concentration
kappas <- c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 3)
 # later add more vals



# store estimated coefficients
beta_linear <- numeric(length(kappas)) # storing linear estimates only
beta_circular <- numeric(length(kappas)) # storing circular estimates only

#for (i in 1:nsim) {
#  results[[i]] <- lm_sim()
#}

# simulation
beta_linear <- beta_circular <- list()
  
nsim <- 100
for (i in 1:length(kappas)) {

  k <- kappas[i] # current iteration
  beta_linear[[i]] <- beta_circular[[i]] <- list()
  for (j in 1:nsim){print(j)
    
  # one predictor to keep it simple
    x <- rnorm(n)
    
    # link function
    mu <- beta0 + 2*atan(beta*x)
    
  # generate circular responses (from previous model)
  y <- sapply(mu, function(m) {
    as.numeric(rvonmises(1, mu = circular(m), kappa = k)) 
  } - pi/2) %% (2*pi) 

  # fit linear regression
  mod1 <- lm(y ~ x)
  beta_linear[[i]][j] <- coef(mod1)[1] + mean(x) * coef(mod1)[2] # saving lin reg coef, [2]=slope
# ^reversing process to get mus
  
  # fit circular regression
  mod2 <- lm.circular(y = circular(y), x = matrix(x, ncol = 1), type = "c-l", init = 0)
  beta_circular[[i]][j] <- mod2$mu + 2*atan(mean(x) * mod2$coefficients[1]) # saving cir reg coef
}}
```


```{r}
data.frame(beta_circ = unlist(lapply(beta_circular, function(x){mean(unlist(x))})),
beta_linear = unlist(lapply(beta_linear, function(x){mean(unlist(x))})), 
kappa = kappas) 


results <- data.frame(beta =  c(unlist(lapply(beta_circular, function(x){mean(unlist(x))})),unlist(lapply(beta_linear, function(x){mean(unlist(x))}))), type = c(rep("circ",length(kappas)),rep("linear",length(kappas))), kappa = rep(kappas,2))

results %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = kappa, y = beta, color = type )) + 
  geom_line()


rose.diag(y, bins = 24, main = paste("kappa =", k))
rose.diag(x, bins = 24, main = paste("kappa =", k))

plot(x,y)

unlist(lapply(beta_circular, function(x){sd(unlist(x))}))



# results
results <- data.frame(kappa = kappas, beta_linear = beta_linear, beta_circular = beta_circular)
results

data.frame(x = x,y =y, r = 1)  %>% ggplot(aes(x = y, y = r, color = x)) + geom_point() + coord_polar() + scale_color_viridis_b()
```

visualizing
```{r}
# linear regression estimates
plot(results$kappa, results$beta_linear, type = "o", col = "deeppink", xlab = "Kappa", ylab = "Estimated Beta", main = "Linear vs Circular Regression", ylim = range(c(results$beta_linear, results$beta_circular)))

# circular regression estimates
lines(results$kappa, results$beta_circular, type = "o", col = "deepskyblue")

# legend
legend("topright", legend = c("Linear", "Circular"), col = c("deeppink", "deepskyblue"), pch = 1)

# true beta 
abline(h = beta, lty = 2)
```

- shift where the ys are and always split at 0
- different kappas, different rotations/splitting points of the ys
- within these bounds (vals of kappa and splitting) you can do a linear regression and it will be okay
- we need to make a region of boundaries 
- convert ys to polar coords
